spec.title: graph2otel Teams
spec.description: Microsoft Teams call, site and service health. Generated from grafana/boards/teams.py.

spec.name: datasource
spec.label: Prometheus datasource
spec.description: Where graph2otel's OTLP metrics land after normalization. Defaults to Grafana Cloud's grafanacloud-prom; pick another Prometheus datasource for a different stack.

spec.name: loki_datasource
spec.label: Loki datasource
spec.description: Required by the log panels. Defaults to Grafana Cloud's grafanacloud-logs. Leave unset and they say so rather than looking broken.

spec.name: tenant
spec.label: Tenant
spec.description: Select the polled tenant; All includes unlabelled single-tenant signals.

spec.name: sites
spec.label: Site
spec.description: Filters the site-labelled stream metrics. All also keeps streams without a mapped site. The exact site search on Calls is the separate Site search box.

spec.name: call_id
spec.label: Call ID
spec.description: Required on Call detail; follows links from call or stream rows.

spec.name: site
spec.label: Site search
spec.description: Exact configured name, either stream side. Used by the Calls site results only.

spec.name: user
spec.label: User UPN
spec.description: Exact observed UPN; call rows check organiser, stream rows check either side.

spec.name: health
spec.label: Call health
spec.description: Exact emitted value (good, poor, or unclassified). Blank means all.

spec.name: call_type
spec.label: Call type
spec.description: Exact Graph type, e.g. peerToPeer or groupCall. Blank means all.

spec.name: modality
spec.label: Modality
spec.description: Exact Graph modality token, e.g. audio or video. Blank means all.

spec.name: min_seconds
spec.label: Minimum duration (seconds)
spec.description: Whole seconds. Blank means all, including unknown duration.

options.content:
Use the panel links for **Call quality** and **Sites and network** trends, or **PSTN and Direct Routing** for phone reports. In **Calls**, filter by duration or observed site, then open a call ID for details. For missing signals, see **Collector health**.

Counters use processing time; logs use source event time. The same range can cover different events on those clocks, and late records can change log counts. Caller endpoints are not a count of distinct people and may not be call initiators.

spec.title: Unique call IDs (event time)
spec.description: Distinct call IDs per tenant by call start time. Exact for keyed Loki records visible in the selected event-time range, not a source census. Late records can change the count. Narrow the range if Loki reaches its series limit. Needs Loki. If it is empty: Teams publishes a call record after the call ends, sometimes hours later. Collector health shows whether the source ran. Log panels also need the Loki datasource.

spec.expr: count by (tenant_id) (sum by (tenant_id, call_id) (count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`teams.call` | tenant_id=~"$tenant" | call_id!=`` | keep tenant_id, call_id [$__auto])))

defaults.noValue: No data yet. See panel info.

spec.title: Call versions (event time)
spec.description: Distinct call ID and version pairs per tenant by call start time. Exact for keyed Loki records visible in the selected event-time range, not a source census. Late records can change the count. Narrow the range if Loki reaches its series limit. Needs Loki. If it is empty: Teams publishes a call record after the call ends, sometimes hours later. Collector health shows whether the source ran. Log panels also need the Loki datasource.

spec.expr: count by (tenant_id) (sum by (tenant_id, call_id, version) (count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`teams.call` | tenant_id=~"$tenant" | call_id!=`` | version!=`` | keep tenant_id, call_id, version [$__auto])))

defaults.noValue: No data yet. See panel info.

spec.title: Calls (collection-time estimate)
spec.description: Health counts the first accepted complete version and is not rewritten by later versions. Estimated counter growth from exported metric samples in the selected collection-time range. Includes the first value of series with no usable baseline at range start; missing samples can distort the estimate. It is not an event-time count. If it is empty: Teams publishes a call record after the call ends, sometimes hours later. Collector health shows whether the source ran.

spec.expr: sum by (tenant_id) (((increase(teams_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range]) or 0 * max_over_time(teams_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range])) + ((min_over_time(teams_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range]) unless teams_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"} offset $__range) or 0 * max_over_time(teams_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range]))))

defaults.noValue: No data yet. See panel info.

spec.title: Good share of classified calls
spec.description: Health counts the first accepted complete version and is not rewritten by later versions. See the coverage table below for the denominator and unclassified count. If it is empty: No positive classified denominator is visible; this is not 0%.

spec.title: Direct Routing attempts (event time)
spec.description: Distinct Direct Routing row IDs per tenant. A row takes its start, invite or failure time, in that order. Exact for keyed Loki records visible in the selected event-time range, not a source census. Late records can change the count. Narrow the range if Loki reaches its series limit. Needs Loki. If it is empty: Teams publishes a call record after the call ends, sometimes hours later. Collector health shows whether the source ran. Log panels also need the Loki datasource.

spec.expr: count by (tenant_id) (sum by (tenant_id, id) (count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`teams.direct_routing_call` | tenant_id=~"$tenant" | id!=`` | keep tenant_id, id [$__auto])))

spec.title: Direct Routing attempts (collection-time estimate)
spec.description: Newly accepted Direct Routing report attempts, including unkeyed rows. Estimated counter growth from exported metric samples in the selected collection-time range. Includes the first value of series with no usable baseline at range start; missing samples can distort the estimate. It is not an event-time count. If it is empty: Teams publishes a call record after the call ends, sometimes hours later. Collector health shows whether the source ran.

spec.expr: sum by (tenant_id) (((increase(teams_direct_routing_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range]) or 0 * max_over_time(teams_direct_routing_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range])) + ((min_over_time(teams_direct_routing_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range]) unless teams_direct_routing_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"} offset $__range) or 0 * max_over_time(teams_direct_routing_calls_total{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}[$__range]))))

spec.title: Microsoft Teams service status
spec.description:
Microsoft's declared status for the Microsoft Teams service, from the service-health collector.

Colour meaning: severity ladder defined by statusEnum in internal/collectors/m365/servicehealth/servicehealth.go, which maps Microsoft's microsoftServiceHealthStatus values onto 0-5 with -1 for an unmapped value. A level Microsoft adds beyond 5 renders as its bare number, which is visible rather than mislabelled. levels 4 and 5 are Microsoft's own serviceDegradation and serviceInterruption: the service is impaired, which is a state Microsoft defines rather than one this repository picked. Levels 1-3 are recovery and investigation, which are not impairment, so they are not coloured. It does not show whether a particular site is affected. If it is empty: No Microsoft Teams status sample is visible. Check Service health and Collector health. Missing status does not mean healthy.

spec.expr: max by (tenant_id) (m365_service_health_status_ratio{tenant_id=~"$tenant",service="Microsoft Teams"})

defaults.noValue: No data yet. See panel info.

spec.title: Recent client bucket counts by platform
spec.description: Initial call counts per client platform, product and version bucket, summed by platform. A call can contribute more than once to a platform. Latest 60 call-end minutes since process start, not a count over the selected range or a count of distinct people or devices. Tenant prefixes are display hints; inspect the series labels for full IDs.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_replace(sum by (tenant_id, platform) (teams_client_versions{tenant_id=~"$tenant"}), "tenant_hint", "$1", "tenant_id", "^(.{1,8}).*$"), "tenant_hint", "unlabelled", "tenant_id", "^$")

spec.title: Observed caller sites
spec.description:
Named sites from the configured mapping, grouped by tenant and site within the recent Loki sample. Unmapped sides are excluded because they name no site. Includes later versions. This is event time; neither the Site metric dropdown nor the metric totals apply here. A site search from a row without a tenant uses All tenants; it does not establish the row's tenant. Up to 250 recent records in the selected time range, not a census.

Needs a **Loki** datasource (selected above). Log attributes are Loki *structured metadata*, not stream labels: filter with `| event_name=…` after `{service_name="graph2otel"}`. A stream selector on an attribute matches zero rows silently (#90).

spec.expr: {service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`teams.call_stream` | tenant_id=~"$tenant" | caller_site!~`unmapped|` | keep tenant_id, caller_site

spec.title: Mapped caller site locations

options.content:
**Find a call:** clear Site search and use health, type, modality, organiser UPN or minimum duration. For example, set health to `poor` and modality to `audio`. Text inputs match exact values.

**Find calls at a site:** enter the exact site name or follow a site link. This searches stream sides, not whole calls. The optional user matches either side; health, type, modality and duration do not apply.

Open a linked call ID to see the same tenant and time window in Call detail. Each table can show multiple versions. When both results are available, use the table's result selector: unlabelled rows remain visible under All tenants but cannot open scoped detail.

spec.title: Call records
spec.description:
One row per observed call version. Poor streams are not a count of affected participants. Up to 250 recent rows per result (labelled or unlabelled) in the selected time range, not a census.

Needs a **Loki** datasource (selected above). Log attributes are Loki *structured metadata*, not stream labels: filter with `| event_name=…` after `{service_name="graph2otel"}`. A stream selector on an attribute matches zero rows silently (#90).

spec.title: Call evidence at the selected site

Counts stored stream rows by stream start in the selected range, not the capped table below. Every counted row has the exact site on either side and has a tenant, call ID and version. spec.title: PSTN report rows (event time)
spec.description: Distinct PSTN row ID, PSTN call ID and start time tuples per tenant, with at least one ID. Row IDs can be shared; this is not a count of unique Teams calls. Exact for keyed Loki records visible in the selected event-time range, not a source census. Late records can change the count. Narrow the range if Loki reaches its series limit. Needs Loki. If it is empty: PSTN and Direct Routing records appear after calls end; healthy_empty means the source answered with no rows. Collector health shows whether the source ran. Log panels also need the Loki datasource.

spec.expr: count by (tenant_id) (sum by (tenant_id, id, call_id, start_time) (count_over_time({service_name="graph2otel"} | event_name=`teams.pstn_call` | tenant_id=~"$tenant" | id != `` or call_id != `` | start_time!=`` | keep tenant_id, id, call_id, start_time [$__auto])))

spec.title: PSTN report rows (collection-time estimate)
spec.description: Newly accepted PSTN report rows, including unkeyed rows. Estimated counter growth from exported metric samples in the selected collection-time range. Includes the first value of series with no usable baseline at range start; missing samples can distort the estimate. It is not an event-time count. If it is empty: PSTN and Direct Routing records appear after calls end; healthy_empty means the source answered with no rows. Collector health shows whether the source ran.

spec.title: Latest exported Direct Routing effectiveness
spec.description: Each sample reflects the most recent available poll value, not a ratio over the selected range. Lookback can repeat a value between observations. Per trunk, the numerator is answered plus busy attempts. The denominator is all newly accepted attempts, including unknowns, not all attempts made. No new attempts means no new ratio. This is not an SBC health check or proof of connected media. Answered means Graph reports successful_call=true, even with SIP 403, which still counts in the 4xx class. Otherwise SIP 486 or 600 is busy. Other explicit failures or SIP 4xx to 6xx are failed; the rest are unknown.

options.content:
Usage comes from Microsoft's daily Teams reports. Platform and activity groups overlap: never add them into a unique-user total.

Usage snapshots in Loki are dated at **UTC midnight on the source refresh date**, not the poll or last activity date. If your range excludes that midnight, an empty result does not mean zero usage or a failed collection. [Find snapshots by refresh date](https://github.com/rknightion/graph2otel/blob/main/docs/signals.md#teams-usage-reports-snapshots-not-activity-events).

spec.title: Teams users by platform (D7)
spec.description: From the Teams device usage report. A user may appear on several platforms; do not sum them.

spec.expr: avg by (tenant_id, platform) (teams_device_usage_users{tenant_id=~"$tenant"})

defaults.noValue: No data yet. Usage reports refresh daily; the first values follow the first report poll. Collector health shows whether the source ran.

spec.title: D7 report refresh date
spec.description: The source refresh date as at the end of the selected range, in UTC (YYYYMMDD). Not a poll time or an activity date. No date is shown if the report did not establish one. If it is empty: Usage reports refresh daily; the first values follow the first report poll. Collector health shows whether the source ran.

spec.expr: year(max by (tenant_id) (m365_teams_usage_report_refresh_timestamp_seconds{tenant_id=~"$tenant",report_period="7"})) * 10000 + month(max by (tenant_id) (m365_teams_usage_report_refresh_timestamp_seconds{tenant_id=~"$tenant",report_period="7"})) * 100 + day_of_month(max by (tenant_id) (m365_teams_usage_report_refresh_timestamp_seconds{tenant_id=~"$tenant",report_period="7"}))

spec.title: Microsoft Teams service status
spec.description:
Microsoft's declared status for the Microsoft Teams service, from the service-health collector.

Colour meaning: severity ladder defined by statusEnum in internal/collectors/m365/servicehealth/servicehealth.go, which maps Microsoft's microsoftServiceHealthStatus values onto 0-5 with -1 for an unmapped value. A level Microsoft adds beyond 5 renders as its bare number, which is visible rather than mislabelled. levels 4 and 5 are Microsoft's own serviceDegradation and serviceInterruption: the service is impaired, which is a state Microsoft defines rather than one this repository picked. Levels 1-3 are recovery and investigation, which are not impairment, so they are not coloured. If it is empty: Needs the m365.servicehealth collector. No issue rows means no Teams issue was observed in range. Collector health shows whether the source ran.

spec.expr: max by (tenant_id) (m365_service_health_status_ratio{tenant_id=~"$tenant",service="Microsoft Teams"})
